title: Wait Queue
body:
[[FIFO]]

The queue of processes blocked on one particular thing. There is a ready queue for the
system; there is a wait queue *per event*: one for each [[Semaphores|semaphore]], one for
each device, one for each condition anybody can block on.

A process enters a wait queue when it blocks, which puts it in the [[Waiting state]]. It
leaves when whatever it was waiting for happens, and it leaves for the [[Ready Queue]], not
straight back onto the CPU.

**FIFO is not decoration.** Waking the longest-waiting process is what gives
[[Bounded Waiting]] its bound, and therefore what stops [[Starvation]]. A wait queue that
woke an arbitrary waiter could leave one thread queued forever while the others cycle
through.

From [[Semaphores]]: the semaphore is a counter *plus* a wait queue. `sem_wait` on a zero
counter appends you here; `sem_post` increments the counter and pulls the front process off
this queue onto the ready queue.

Contrast with the [[Ready Queue]]: everyone in a wait queue is unable to run, everyone in
the ready queue is able to run and simply is not scheduled yet. See [[Process State]].
